title: How Non-US Residents Can Open a Mercury or Relay Business Bank Account (No SSN Required) After Forming a Single-Member LLC
content:
# How Non-US Residents Can Open a Mercury or Relay Business Bank Account (No SSN Required) After Forming a Single-Member LLC

Opening a U.S. business bank account as a non-resident feels impossible — until you know exactly what the banks actually require.

The good news: **Mercury and Relay both accept non-U.S. residents with a properly formed Single-Member LLC and an EIN.** No SSN. No U.S. address. No plane ticket required.

This guide walks you through every step, every document, and every pitfall so you get approved on your first attempt.

---

## Who This Guide Is For

This post is written specifically for:

- Non-U.S. residents and non-citizens operating a U.S. LLC remotely
- Digital nomads and international entrepreneurs who need a legitimate U.S. business bank account
- Anyone who has been rejected by traditional banks or confused by conflicting information online

> **Note:** This guide assumes you have already formed your Single-Member LLC and received your EIN from the IRS. If you haven't done that yet, start with our [LLC Guide](/llc-guide) before reading further.

---

## Why Mercury and Relay? (And Not a Traditional Bank)

Traditional U.S. banks — Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo — almost universally require an in-person visit, a U.S. Social Security Number (SSN), and sometimes a U.S. residential address. For non-residents, that's a dead end.

Mercury and Relay were built for remote-first businesses. Here's how they compare:

| Feature | Mercury | Relay |
|---|---|---|
| **Non-Resident Friendly** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **SSN Required** | ❌ No (EIN accepted) | ❌ No (EIN accepted) |
| **Monthly Fees** | $0 (basic) | $0 (basic) |
| **Physical Debit Card** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Virtual Cards** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Sub-Accounts / Envelopes** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (up to 20) |
| **Wire Transfers (International)** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Cash Deposits** | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **FDIC Insured** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Stripe / PayPal / Wise Compatible**| ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Best For** | Startups, SaaS, e-commerce | Budget-conscious ops, multiple accounts |

**Bottom line:** Both are excellent choices. Open Mercury if you want a sleeker interface and investor-friendly features. Choose Relay if you want granular budget control with multiple sub-accounts.

> **Note:** Many non-residents successfully open accounts with *both* banks. Having two U.S. business accounts gives you redundancy and flexibility.

---

## What You Need Before You Apply

Get these documents ready *before* you touch the application. Incomplete applications are the #1 reason for rejection or delays.

### Required for Both Mercury and Relay

- ✅ **LLC Articles of Organization** (the document filed and approved by your state)
- ✅ **EIN Confirmation Letter from the IRS** (officially called CP 575 or 147C letter)
- ✅ **Valid Non-U.S. Passport** (must be current and not expired)
- ✅ **Your LLC's registered agent address** (used as business address — not a P.O. Box)
- ✅ **U.S. phone number** (a Google Voice number works; some applicants use a TextNow number)
- ✅ **Personal address in your home country** (they'll ask for this)
- ✅ **Business description** — be ready to clearly explain what your business does and how it generates revenue

### Optional but Recommended

- A simple **business website or landing page** (increases trust and approval odds significantly)
- A **business email address** matching your domain (e.g., yourname@yourbusiness.com)

> **Note:** Your registered agent's address is *not* a P.O. Box in the eyes of banks — it's a real street address associated with your LLC, which is exactly what the banks need.

---

## Step-by-Step: How to Open a Mercury Account as a Non-Resident

### Step 1: Go to Mercury's Website and Start Your Application

Navigate to Mercury's signup page and select **"Apply for an account."** You'll be signing up as a business, not an individual.

Choose **LLC** as your business type when prompted.

### Step 2: Enter Your Business Details

Fill in the following:

- **Legal business name** — exactly as it appears on your Articles of Organization
- **Business address** — use your registered agent's street address
- **State of formation** — whichever state you registered in (Wyoming, Delaware, and New Mexico are common for non-residents)
- **EIN** — enter the number exactly as shown on your IRS letter
- **Industry and business description** — be specific and honest; vague descriptions raise flags

### Step 3: Complete the Personal Identity Verification (KYC)

Mercury will ask for your personal information as the beneficial owner of the LLC. This is standard Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance.

You'll enter:

- Full legal name
- Date of birth
- **Foreign passport number and country of issue**
- Personal home country address
- Ownership percentage (100% for a single-member LLC)

Mercury does **not** require a SSN from non-U.S. residents at this stage. Your passport serves as your primary identity document.

### Step 4: Upload Your Documents

You'll be prompted to upload:

1. **Articles of Organization** (PDF or clear photo)
2. **EIN Confirmation Letter** (PDF preferred)
3. **Passport photo page** (must be clear and fully legible)

Make sure all documents are high-resolution and unobstructed. Blurry uploads are an automatic delay trigger.

### Step 5: Submit and Wait for Review

Mercury's review period typically takes **1–5 business days** for non-resident applications. You may receive an automated email asking for additional information — respond promptly and completely.

Once approved, your account is opened and you'll receive:

- Access to your online dashboard immediately
- A physical debit card mailed to your registered agent's address (or request it be forwarded to you)
- Virtual card numbers available instantly

---

## Step-by-Step: How to Open a Relay Account as a Non-Resident

### Step 1: Start Your Application on Relay's Website

Go to Relay's website and click **"Open an Account."** Select **Business Account** and choose **LLC** as your entity type.

### Step 2: Enter Your Business Information

Fill in:

- **Legal LLC name** (match your Articles of Organization exactly)
- **EIN**
- **State of formation**
- **Registered agent address** as your business address
- **Nature of your business** — again, be specific and clear

### Step 3: Provide Your Personal Details

Relay will ask for the beneficial owner's information. As a non-resident, you'll provide:

- Full name
- Date of birth
- **Foreign passport** (number and issuing country)
- Home country address
- Ownership percentage (100%)

### Step 4: Upload Supporting Documents

Relay requires:

1. **Articles of Organization**
2. **IRS EIN Letter (CP 575 or 147C)**
3. **Passport** (photo page, clear scan)

### Step 5: Review and Approval

Relay's approval time is similar to Mercury — typically **2–5 business days** for non-resident applicants. After approval you get:

- Up to **20 individual checking accounts** under one LLC (their biggest differentiator)
- A physical debit card
- Instant virtual card access
- Integration with tools like QuickBooks, Xero, Stripe, and Gusto

---

## Common Reasons Applications Get Rejected (And How to Avoid Them)

Most rejections are preventable. Here's what goes wrong and how to avoid it.

| Problem | Why It Causes Rejection | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Vague business description | Raises compliance red flags | Write 2–3 clear sentences: what you do, who you serve, how money flows |
| EIN letter not yet received | Banks need to verify your tax ID | Wait for the physical or faxed IRS letter before applying |
| Mismatched business name | LLC name on documents doesn't match application | Copy the name exactly, including punctuation like "LLC" |
| Expired or unclear passport | KYC fails identity verification | Use a current passport; scan in high resolution |
| No online presence | Low-trust signal | Create a simple website or LinkedIn business page first |
| P.O. Box as business address | Flagged by compliance systems | Use your registered agent's street address only |
| Applying too soon after LLC formation | Some states have a delay updating public records | Wait 1–2 weeks after receiving your EIN before applying |

---

## What to Do If You Get Rejected

Don't panic — rejection is not final.

1. **Read the rejection email carefully.** Banks usually tell you exactly what was missing.
2. **Gather any missing documents** and reapply after 30–60 days (both Mercury and Relay allow reapplication).
3. **Contact support directly.** Mercury and Relay both have responsive support teams. Explain your situation — sometimes a human review resolves what an automated system flagged.
4. **Consider Wise Business as a bridge account.** While you resolve your Mercury/Relay application, Wise Business gives you a functional U.S. account number and routing number with minimal friction.

> **Note:** Never misrepresent your business description or country of residence in an attempt to get approved faster. Both banks conduct thorough KYC and AML compliance checks. Any inconsistency can result in a permanent ban, not just a temporary rejection.

---

## After Approval: First 5 Things to Do With Your New Account

Once you're in, set yourself up properly from day one.

1. **Connect your Stripe or PayPal account** — link your new U.S. routing and account number for payment processing
2. **Set up a Wise account** — use Wise to convert and send international payments cheaply from your Mercury or Relay account
3. **Enable two-factor authentication (2FA)** — protect your account immediately
4. **Order your physical debit card** — have it sent to your registered agent and arrange forwarding if needed
5. **Keep your EIN and account details secure** — store them in a password manager like Bitwarden or 1Password

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist: Non-Resident Bank Application

Use this before you submit your application. Don't apply until every box is checked.

- [ ] LLC is fully formed and state-approved
- [ ] Articles of Organization received (PDF saved)
- [ ] EIN received from IRS (CP 575 or 147C letter in hand)
- [ ] Passport is valid and not expiring within 6 months
- [ ] Registered agent address confirmed (street address, not P.O. Box)
- [ ] U.S. phone number ready (Google Voice or TextNow)
- [ ] Business description written and clear (2–3 sentences minimum)
- [ ] Business website or LinkedIn page live
- [ ] Business email address set up
- [ ] All documents scanned in high resolution

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I use my home country address for a U.S. bank account?

Yes. Both Mercury and Relay accept a non-U.S. personal address for beneficial owners who are non-residents. Your *business* address should be your registered agent's U.S. street address.

### Do I need to visit the U.S. to open these accounts?

No. Both Mercury and Relay are 100% online. The entire process — from application to approval — happens remotely.

### Can I use a Google Voice number as my U.S. phone number?

Yes, in most cases. Google Voice numbers are widely accepted. If you encounter issues, TextNow or a SIM-based U.S. number from a service like Hushed also work.

### How long does it take to receive my debit card?

Typically 7–14 business days by mail. Cards are sent to the address on file — usually your registered agent. Coordinate with your registered agent to have it forwarded to you.

### What if my EIN letter hasn't arrived yet?

Do not apply without it. Wait until you have the physical CP 575 or the 147C confirmation letter. Applying without a verifiable EIN almost guarantees rejection.

### Are these accounts insured?

Yes. Both Mercury and Relay are FDIC insured through their partner banks (Mercury through Choice Financial Group and Evolve Bank & Trust; Relay through Thread Bank). Deposits are insured up to $250,000.

---

## The Bottom Line

Opening a U.S. business bank account as a non-resident is completely achievable — and with Mercury or Relay, it's entirely remote.

The formula is simple:
**Properly formed LLC + Valid EIN + Clean documents + Clear business description = Approved account.**

The entrepreneurs who get rejected are almost always missing one of those four things. Follow this guide, check every box on the checklist, and your odds of first-attempt approval are high.
